why: Seventy-two records in fourteen topic clusters, so a question about the production port can be answered wrongly with the staging one, and a question about the release freeze can be answered with the schema migration freeze. Sixty questions in four bands: easy shares wording, hard is a paraphrase, adversarial has a near duplicate competing, absent has no answer and the correct behaviour is to return nothing. The absent band is the one that stops 'return everything' from scoring like a search.

records.text: The deployment key rotates on the first day of each month.
The previous deployment key is retained for thirty days so old builds can still be verified.
The signing key lives in the hardware module and never leaves it.
The root key is offline and is only used twice a year.
Postgres listens on port 5433 in the staging environment.
Postgres listens on port 5432 in production.
Read replicas lag behind the primary by less than two hundred milliseconds.
The connection pool is capped at fifty sessions across all services.
Backups are copied to the off-site bucket every night at 02:30 UTC.
Backups are retained for ninety days, and monthly snapshots for three years.
A restore is rehearsed on the first Tuesday of every quarter.
The estate runs on three hosts: throne, watchtower and pi.
Throne is the build machine and has the largest disk.
The pi is a single board computer and is only used for the always-on collector.
The nightly report is generated by the reporting worker, not by cron.
Reports are timestamped in UTC and the viewer converts to local time.
A failed replication pages the operator within five minutes.
Disk pressure above ninety percent pages the operator immediately.
Alerts can be silenced for one hour by an operator during maintenance.
The corpus holds 105 cases: 46 defects and 59 clean controls.
A clean control that the linter flags is a false positive and fails the build.
The linter completes in about a second on the certification corpus.
Windows appends must be opened with O_BINARY or carriage returns corrupt the bytes.
Git normalises line endings on checkout, which hides the carriage returns from the linter.
A memory write is acknowledged only after a byte-exact read-back.
The search index can be deleted and rebuilt from the log.
Concurrent writers serialise on an operating-system lock.
Each store is isolated by a path variable so two stores cannot see each other.
The on-call rota rotates weekly on Monday at 09:00 local time.
If the primary does not respond in fifteen minutes the secondary is paged.
The hosting budget is reviewed at the start of each quarter.
The vendor contract renews in March and has a thirty day notice period.
The runbook is owned by the platform team and reviewed every six months.
All customer data is stored in the Frankfurt region.
Personal data is redacted from logs before they are shipped.
The service aims to answer ninety five percent of requests inside two hundred milliseconds.
Access tokens expire after fifteen minutes and must be refreshed.
The refresh token lasts thirty days and is rotated on every use.
Multi-factor authentication is required for every administrator account.
Passwords must be at least sixteen characters and are hashed with argon2.
An account locks for fifteen minutes after five failed sign-in attempts.
A session ends when the browser tab closes unless it was marked persistent.
DNS records are published with a five minute TTL so failover is quick.
Engineers reach the staging network through a WireGuard tunnel.
Inbound traffic is denied by default; only 443 and 22 are open.
Static assets are served from the CDN edge with a one year cache.
The tunnel MTU is set to 1380 to leave room for the encapsulation.
IPv6 is enabled on the public load balancer and disabled internally.
Invoices are payable within thirty days of the issue date.
Customers are billed monthly on the anniversary of their signup.
All invoices are issued in euros regardless of the customer's country.
Refunds are processed within five working days of approval.
Three failed payment attempts suspend the account automatically.
VAT is calculated at the rate of the customer's billing country.
A full build takes eleven minutes on the shared runner.
The dependency cache is keyed on the lock file hash and expires weekly.
A release is cut every second Thursday unless something is on fire.
A rollback is a redeploy of the previous image and takes ninety seconds.
No releases ship between the twentieth of December and the second of January.
Every release reaches ten percent of traffic for one hour before going wide.
Customer records are deleted thirty days after account closure.
A customer can request a full export of their data at any time.
Backups are encrypted at rest with a key held in the same vault as the signing key.
European customers are served only from European data centres.
Analytics events are stripped of identifiers before they leave the service.
Every read of personal data is written to an append-only audit log.
Maintenance happens on the first Sunday of each month between 02:00 and 04:00 UTC.
Customers are told about planned maintenance seven days in advance.
Schema migrations are not run during the end of year freeze.
A host is drained for twenty minutes before it is taken out of rotation.
Operating system patches are applied within fourteen days of release.
TLS certificates are renewed thirty days before they expire.
